sources.text:
BIOGRAPHY / 创作简介
何发
摄影、剧场与电影
何发是跨媒介艺术创作者、剧场与影像创作者，P4剧场共同发起人、长期主理人与组织者。2012年完成摄影作品《山重水复》；2015年前后与张绍华在北京共同发起P4剧场；2023至2024年执导电影《人类投降派》。他的工作穿行于摄影、现场、电影与声音之间。
历史文献中的Fa He亦为何发。现用英文署名He Fa。
HF
HE FA / 何发
艺术家肖像
创作经历
何发的创作从摄影开始。2012年的《山重水复》由大量局部照片拼接而成。远看是一幅山水，靠近之后，画面重新分散成不同时间、焦点和拍摄位置。观看者需要不断靠近、退后，才能在整体与细节之间辨认这件作品。
在旧金山的《Fafalish》（2017）中，文字、口音和听写让一句话经过多次转换；《YourTube》（2018）把图像与弹幕带回相连座位和屏幕构成的空间。在北京的《实像》中，拍摄与观看则成为多次会面之间交替进行的行动。这些作品让语言、身体距离与他人的在场进入图像内部。
2012年，何发共同创办格物工作室并担任艺术总监，在《十二水灯》等共同实践中承担摄影、概念构思、造型探索与艺术指导。这段经历把图像、物件与空间带入同一条创作线索。
2015年前后，何发与张绍华在北京共同发起P4剧场。张傲霜参与早期构想，并与何发共同策划2016年的首场公开演出《影子对位法》。何发此后长期担任P4的主理人与组织者，项目进入过废弃厂房、十几平方米的办公室、拳击空间、书店与私人居所。
《天台上的嚎叫者》于2021年1月2日在P4公演；《冰山》于2022年1月1日在狭小办公室中向15位观众演出；《决斗俱乐部》于2021年10月23日在北京朝阳的拳击空间公演。何发在这些项目中的工作分别涉及P4组织、3P现场记录、制作与共同推进。
2023年8月26日，《最后的排练》在刺鱼书店（中间剧场店）演出，现场材料随后进入《人类投降派》。2024年，何发完成约156分钟的电影版本；此后继续整理人物声音、对白、电影帧、短片与文字。何发：导演、发起、制片、剪辑；导演与编剧由剧组成员共同创作。

sources.title: He Fa Photography, theatre and film
sources.text:
BIOGRAPHY / ARTISTIC PRACTICE
He Fa
Photography, theatre and film
He Fa is an interdisciplinary artist and a theatre and moving-image maker. He is a co-initiator and the long-term artistic lead and organiser of P4 Theater. He completed Mountain Beyond Mountains (Shanshui / 山重水复) in 2012, initiated P4 Theater in Beijing with Zhang Shaohua around 2015, and directed Human Surrender / Shoot Self with You in 2023–2024. His work moves through photography, live situations, film and sound.
Fa He in historical records also refers to He Fa, the English name used here.
HF
HE FA / 何发
ARTIST PORTRAIT
Artistic practice
He Fa began with photography. Mountain Beyond Mountains (2012) is assembled from many partial photographs. From a distance it reads as a landscape; at close range it separates into different times, focal points and camera positions. The viewer has to move back and forth to read the work between whole and detail.
In Fafalish (2017), made in San Francisco, writing, accent and listening carry a sentence through successive transformations. YourTube (2018) brings images and comments into a space of screens and connected seats. In Shixiang, developed in Beijing, photographing and viewing alternate across repeated encounters. Language, bodily distance and other people’s presence become part of the image.
In 2012, He Fa co-founded Gewu Studio and served as its artistic director. His work within collaborative projects including Twelve Water Lamps encompassed photography, conceptual development, form exploration and artistic direction. This period brought images, objects and space into a shared line of inquiry.
Around 2015, He Fa and Zhang Shaohua initiated P4 Theater in Beijing. Zhang Aoshuang joined its early conception and co-curated the first public performance, Shadow Counterpoint, with He Fa in 2016. He Fa has since continued as P4’s long-term artistic lead and organiser, working in former factories, a small office, a boxing space, bookstores and private rooms.
Howlers on the Rooftop was performed at P4 on 2 January 2021; Iceberg was performed for fifteen spectators inside a small office on 1 January 2022; and Duel Club took place in a boxing space in Chaoyang, Beijing, on 23 October 2021. He Fa’s work across them involved P4 organisation, 3P live documentation, production and collaborative development.
The Last Rehearsal took place at Ciyu Bookstore (Middle Theater branch) on 26 August 2023, and material from the event entered Human Surrender / Shoot Self with You. He Fa completed an approximately 156-minute film cut in 2024 and has since continued to work with its voices, dialogue, frames, short films and writing. He Fa: director, initiator, producer and editor; direction and screenplay were collectively created by the crew.

HE FA / FA HE / 何发
Work records & citation
Titles, dates, media, credits and sources.
He Fa is the English name currently used by the artist 何发. Historical records also use Fa He for the same person. Based in Beijing, he works across photography, moving-image installations, theatre and film, and is a co-initiator and long-term host of P4 Theater.
Organised by each work’s place and significance within the practice, with completed works and research in progress identified. Developed early and co-authored works, alongside current projects with concrete research material, can appear in the selection. Early explorations, sustained collaborative practice and proposals have separate entrances.

sources.title: 何发的 艺术实践
sources.text:
何发 · 创作档案 · 中文全文
Chinese original
咔馆 · 创作档案　/　2026.10
何发的
艺术实践
从摄影拼贴、语言实验
到P4剧场与集体电影
一座山，不一定来自一个固定的观看位置。一张肖像，也不一定在快门落下时完成。
01 / 何发，《山重水复——红》，2012。数字摄影拼贴。
作品与图像资料 ↗
在何发的作品中，摄影可以成为重新构造风景的方法，也可以成为下一次见面的理由；语言的错误可以被保留下来，继续生成新的语言；一次招募、几周排练、一场讨论和一段没有顺利完成的表演，都可能进入作品的形成过程。理解他的实践，需要同时看见两个方面：他如何制作具体的图像、物件与影像，以及他如何组织让这些东西得以发生的人、空间和时间。
何发出生并成长于江苏淮安，2008至2012年就读于中央美术学院，学习摄影，后于2016至2018年在加州艺术学院——California College of the Arts，简称CCA——进行纯艺术研究生阶段的学习。
他是P4剧场联合创始人，创作涉及摄影、数字拼贴、设计、语言实验、影像装置、参与式剧场与电影。其间既有个人作品，也有与其他艺术家合作的项目，以及通过策划、制作、记录和组织参与的集体实践。
[1]
把这段经历概括为“从摄影转向戏剧，再转向电影”，虽然方便，却容易错过真正重要的联系。摄影没有在剧场出现后被放弃；剧场也不只是电影之前的准备。它们彼此进入、相互改写，但始终保留着各自不同的问题。
何发的实践，可以从一个持续变化的工作方向来理解：既要做出具有自身形式的作品，也要让作品的形成过程能够遇到他人的行动、回应与不确定性。
这两者并不总是协调一致，而它们之间的张力，正是其创作值得具体讨论的地方。
01 /
摄影
重新做出一个整体
何发早期摄影的核心，并不是寻找一个足以概括世界的决定性瞬间，而是把不同位置、不同时间拍下的照片重新组织起来。在这一过程中，照片既保留着对现实的指涉，也成为可以移动、叠加、排列和改变尺度的材料。
《山重水复》（2012）是这一阶段的重要作品。远看时，观众面对的是一幅具有山水形态的整体；走近之后，构成山体的局部照片逐渐显现。整体风景与局部图像并非同一种观看经验：前者使人辨认出山势、空间与气氛，后者则让人意识到，这座山由许多次并不完整的观察构成。
作品档案还保存了网格色彩组织、主观排列、叠加、位移与透明度调整等制作方法，说明它并不是把照片随意堆积在一起，而是让规则与视觉判断共同参与构图。

03 / 《山重水复》工作目录中的横向拼合过程图。具体制作时间未定。
这里的重要之处，不只是“用了很多照片”，也不只是“摄影看起来像山水画”。照片从原来的拍摄场景中被取出之后，开始承担新的形式功能：某张照片的明暗、颜色、边界与纹理，可以成为另一座山的组成部分。作品最终形成的整体，既不等于任何一张原始照片，也不是某个固定视点下的景观复原。
因此，拼贴在这里不是单纯的破碎化。相反，它包含一种很强的整体构造欲望：让来源不同的图像成为一个能够被观看、能够建立自身秩序的世界，同时又让这个世界的接缝保持可见。
中央美术学院美术馆的2012届毕业生作品收藏记录，列有何发的《山重水复——红》《山重水复——白》，媒介为C-print灯箱片与灯箱，每件尺寸为110×190厘米。这一记录也提醒我们：这些作品不是只存在于屏幕上的数字拼图，而是具有实际尺度、亮度和观看距离的摄影作品。
[3]
与风景拼贴相对应，《我》及其前后的肖像版本，把身体本身变成了需要重新辨认的对象。面部不再只是一个迅速确认身份的符号，而成为可以被局部拍摄、放大和重新拼合的表面。远处仍然能够辨认出一个人，近处却遇到构成这个人的摄影材料。作品没有简单消除肖像的整体性，而是使整体与局部之间不再完全吻合。

格物
形体、材料与光怎样共同工作
2012年，何发与宋波纹共同创办格物工作室，进入艺术产品、参数化设计与3D打印相关实践。这一经历不能被视为摄影与剧场之间的一段无关插曲，因为它把图像构成的问题带到了实体材料之中：一个形体如何生成，褶皱、开口、厚度与内部光源如何形成相互依赖的整体。

Fafalish
把口音、误听与翻译变成创作材料
在Fafalish，即“发发语言”项目中，何发把摄影中的重新排列扩展到语言，但这并不是简单地把词语像照片一样拼在一起。他建立的是一个让文字、声音、身体和工具连续介入的转换过程。
16 / Fafalish 现场工作记录。原文件 DSC02869.JPG；EXIF日期2017-10-24。
作品与图像资料 ↗
以2017年的影像《Kunlun (Brother Order)》为例，作品以中文诗词为起点，将汉字逐字转换成英文，再以带有中文口音的英语朗读；随后，声音又被当作近似汉语拼音的材料来辨听，重新对应成汉字，最后借助机器翻译转换为英文。意义并没有经过一圈转换后回到原处，而是在每一个环节中发生偏移。CCA的机构档案具体记录了这一过程。
[5]
17 / Fafalish 字典实验三屏过程图。艺术家自存文件；具体制作时间待确认。
这种做法的关键，并不是证明翻译“不准确”。通常被语言训练排除的东西——口音、误读、听觉联想、机器的错误——在这里被保留为下一步工作的材料。说话者不必先成为一个掌握标准语言的人，才能开始表达；语言的偏差本身就参与了表达的生成。
同时，Fafalish并不只是纸面上的文字游戏。2017年10月2日至12月15日，该项目在CCA旧金山校区的Simpson Library展出，将影像与纸上文字装置带入图书馆的阅读环境。展览档案中的长墙文字、平板与耳机，使语言分别以行走阅读、屏幕观看和个人聆听的方式出现。
文字与声音没有被压缩成一种统一的解释，而是要求观看者在不同媒介之间转换。

从方法上看，这件作品使“沟通失败”获得了不同的位置。失败不再只是需要被纠正的障碍，也可能成为继续创作的条件。但这并不意味着误解天然具有解放性：陌生的文字既可能打开新的感知，也可能成为难以进入的屏障。作品的力量，恰恰在于让这两种可能同时存在。

YourTube
屏幕连接了什么，又把什么分开
2018年的《YourTube》进一步把语言、网络影像和观看空间联系起来。根据作品布展档案，装置包括六台显像管电视、五台平板屏幕，以及六个由彩色管道连接的座位。屏幕分布在不同高度，座位形成相互连接的结构，观看不再围绕一块正面的银幕展开。

P4的形成
图像开始面对会回应的人
P4的历史，需要把共同发起、空间建设和正式开放区分开来。现行档案将其起点追溯到2015年前后，何发与张绍华共同发起，张傲霜参与了早期剧场构想及相关创作。2016年6月4日，位于北京雕塑台工作室内的P4正式对外开放；同期中央美术学院艺术资讯网的报道，明确记载何发与傲霜共同策划实验戏剧《影子对位法》。

从早期空间说明就可以看出，P4并不是一个与摄影无关的戏剧场所。黑色帷幕、拍摄区域、表演区域以及身体被观看的位置，原本就构成了其空间设想。影像与戏剧的关系，不是后来才附加上去的跨界装饰，而是这个空间最初要处理的问题之一。
[8]
何发与张傲霜合作的《哈姆雷特的镜子》，提供了这一问题的具体形式。其早期版本围绕屏幕、表演者、投影机与摄影机展开，使身体既参与表演，也进入影像的形成与遮蔽过程。观众面对的不只是一个正在表演的人，还包括这个人如何变成图像，以及身体与图像之间不能完全重合的关系。

实像
照片不是终点，而是下一次相见的条件
2019年6月，何发与张绍华开始《实像》项目。它以肖像拍摄为入口，却没有把目标限定为完成一张“最像本人”的照片，而是将谈话、拍摄、选片、回看与后续参与连接起来。项目的公开招募文案称其为“两个人的戏剧，只为再见你”。
[10]

在《实像》中，被拍摄者首先是一个来到现场的人，而不是等待摄影师调整姿势的对象。面对面的相处与谈话构成了工作的重要部分。2021年的专业媒体访谈中，张绍华与何发介绍了这种没有预先固定剧本的见面方式：有人讲述经历，有人带着强烈情绪，也有人保持沉默。摄影发生在这样的相处之中，而不是将相处视为进入“正式拍摄”之前可以省略的准备。
[11]

《实像》最鲜明的安排，是让前一次拍摄的照片进入下一次见面。照片没有立即完成它的全部用途，而是带着上一次的时间，成为新的谈话对象。参与者也可以决定是否继续，以及照片是否公开；在当时的招募方案中，不继续参与的人可以通过邮寄收到照片。

这使肖像发生了一种结构变化。照片一方面固定了过去的姿态，另一方面又被带到一个已经变化的人面前。这个人可以认同照片，也可以觉得陌生，可以重新理解当时的自己，也可以拒绝让一张照片概括自己的全部。

因此，《实像》并不是用摄影证明一个人终于显露了“真正的自我”，而是让人、照片和下一次相见之间保持可讨论的关系。照片的固执与人的变化，在这里同时起作用。
项目曾设计“八部半”的长期结构，但这一设计不等于已经完成八个半阶段。2021年访谈时，尚无完成全部阶段的参与样本；后来的自述也保留了项目未走完原定结构的事实。这种未完成不应被抹去，因为它使作品中“再次相见”的愿望与现实中的时间、合作和离开之间的距离显现出来。

同样，参与者可能获得安慰、理解或新的自我认识，但这些体验不宜被写成已经证实的心理治疗效果。《实像》的艺术意义，首先在于它如何组织观看与相遇，而不是它是否能够保证某一种结果。

组织与制作
招募、排练、制作与记录
何发的实践不能只通过个人署名的成品来介绍。P4的招募机制、排练安排、放映与讨论、作品制作以及过程记录，同样构成了他长期投入的工作。
2020年的P4U招募文件提出，以项目形式召集创作者与参与者，在一定周期内共同工作，并将公开呈现作为明确的时间节点。参与并不以专业艺术学历为唯一门槛，但项目也保留选择、组织和判断机制。同时，从招募到公演的过程被纳入记录工作，由黄麓苍、张绍华、何发组成的3P记录组参与。
[12]
39 / 《天台上的嚎叫者》“七十七岁的小女孩”访谈配图：灯光与夹层空间。
作品与图像资料 ↗
这种结构与“大家自由发挥”并不是一回事。
当公演日期确定下来，参与者就必须面对一系列实际决定：谁来提出材料，谁来表演，某段内容是否保留，意见不一致时如何继续，什么时候停止讨论，什么时候把一个方案落实为动作。作品不只由台上的内容组成，也由这些决定逐渐形成。
40 / 《天台上的嚎叫者》参与者zaoyi；2021年访谈配图。
作品与图像资料 ↗
41 / 《天台上的嚎叫者》“七十七岁的小女孩”访谈配图：椅子与身体。
作品与图像资料 ↗
在这个意义上，何发的工作有时更接近搭建生产条件：找到能够一起工作的人，提供空间与设备，使一个还没有完整形态的想法获得时间，推动它进入排练，再使排练中的材料能够被观看和整理。但这样的组织并不意味着作者权力消失。谁设定项目目标，谁拥有最后的选择权，仍然是创作结构的一部分。
不同项目中，何发承担的角色也不能混为一谈。《天台上的嚎叫者》涉及P4组织与3P现场记录；《冰山》中，他承担制作工作；《破月》中，他是监制，导演为徐帅。将这些工作一律写成“何发导演作品”是不准确的；反过来，因为不是独立导演就忽略这些贡献，也同样无法解释作品如何实际发生。
[1]
42 / 《冰山》现场记录。北风剧社集体创作；何发承担制作工作。
作品与图像资料 ↗
43 / 《破月》演前海报，2023。导演徐帅，监制何发。保留原海报中的主创署名与历史演出信息。
作品与图像资料 ↗
44 / 《破月》表演相关照片，原刊于2023年12月7日的演员介绍。
作品与图像资料 ↗
P4后来离开原有空间，继续在更小的场所中展开实践，也使制作条件直接进入了作品。小空间不仅意味着资源限制，还意味着不同的观看距离、身体尺度和现场压力。不过，接近并不自动产生亲密，人数少也不自动意味着更深的交流。这些都需要通过具体的排练与空间组织才能成立。
[13]
45 / 510阶段的桌边工作场景，2023。桌面、黑帘和近距离的杂物构成实际工作空间。
何发曾用“用假撬动真”概括P4的工作方向。这里的“假”，可以理解为被制作出来的角色、台词、场景和规则；“真”则不是对未经加工生活的简单复制，而是在这些条件中真正发生的行动与经验。一个人可以借别人的台词说出自己此前说不出的话，也可以通过一个角色，第一次以不同的方式面对另一个人。与此同时，预设情境只能提供可能，不能保证结果。
[14]
08 /
参与式实验
观众进入了作品，也进入了规则
何发与沈博伦、邵逸凡共同参与的紫色行动及相关项目，把组织问题进一步推进到规则本身。这里的参与者不只是被邀请上台完成某个动作，观看者的判断、投票和选择，也可能进入现场的进程。
[15]
46 / 紫色行动项目预告片片尾，2021。保留原片画面。
作品与图像资料 ↗
47 / 紫色行动历史现场。2021年10月19日招募文配图，早于10月23日决斗俱乐部活动。
作品与图像资料 ↗
48 / 紫色行动历史现场。2021年10月19日招募文配图，早于10月23日决斗俱乐部活动。
作品与图像资料 ↗
2021年10月23日举行的“星期六四小时决斗俱乐部”，是一个具体例子。演出设置在拳击场环境中，由六位“斗士”进入四小时的竞逐，观众通过投票参与决定结果。参与者的表达与现场竞争被放进同一套结构，观看不再只是对一个已经完成的故事作出评价，而是能够影响事件下一步如何进行。
[15]
49 / 2021 年 10 月 23 日《决斗俱乐部》公开海报。
作品与图像资料 ↗
在这样的项目中，规则本身就是一种戏剧材料。一个人如何争取注意，怎样解释自己，观众为什么支持某个人，主持者怎样安排发言与投票，都可能比某个预先写好的情节更直接地形成冲突。公开保存的现场文字记录，还能看到投票时段、发言机会与票数资源等具体环节如何进入表演。
[16]
因此，这类工作不宜被简单称为“消除观演边界”。边界并没有消失，而是发生了变化：原来不需要作决定的观众，现在需要对自己的选择承担某种位置；原来只是表演者的人，也可能必须面对竞争、比较和被淘汰。
同样，参与不等于平等，投票也不自动解决权力问题。规则由谁设计，谁能解释规则，谁拥有更多表达机会，仍然需要被具体观察。保留这些问题，不是在否定项目，而是在承认它真正进入了社会关系，而不只是借用了“参与”的外观。
《个人志》中的PHA框架与公共记录设想，以及《幸福王国》中围绕角色、物件和玩法进行的共同设计，又把这一方向带向不同形式。它们分别涉及个人经验如何被建档、角色如何被共同生成，以及一套设定怎样在持续使用中发生变化。不能因为这些项目都与参与有关，就把它们归纳成同一种已经成熟的模式。
[1]
[17]
50 / 《个人志》原始概念图，2023。
作品与图像资料 ↗
51 / 《幸福王国》造偶与场景，2023 年 4 月公开图像。
作品与图像资料 ↗
52 / 《幸福王国》角色与造物；具体单件制作者未在图片中标明。
作品与图像资料 ↗
09 /
人类投降派
让拍摄关系进入电影
《人类投降派》，英文名为
Shoot Self with You
，集中呈现了何发的剧场实践与电影工作之间的关系。
这一项目从招募、排练与拍摄阶段就具有电影计划，而不是在一部戏剧完成之后，才将演出录像重新命名为电影。2023年的排练、拍摄和现场表演共同构成其材料来源；2023年8月26日，《最后的排练》在刺鱼书店中间剧场店公开呈现，与后续电影相连接。2024年，项目形成约156分钟的电影版本。
[18]
[1]
53 / 《最后的排练》公演海报；演出于2023年8月26日在刺鱼书店（中间剧场店）举行。
作品与图像资料 ↗
54 / 《人类投降派》电影帧，00:07:49。三个身体在近距离内构成对话关系。
作品与图像资料 ↗
影片的详细署名尤其重要。按现行作品档案，导演与编剧由剧组成员集体承担，何发的核心工作包括发起、制片与剪辑，并参与摄影、艺术指导等环节。部分对外数据库使用Fa He作为导演登记，并不适合用来覆盖更具体的集体创作署名。
[19]
[1]
55 / 片尾02:34:12：发起人与导演、编剧的集体署名。
作品与图像资料 ↗
56 / 片尾02:34:50：制作、剪辑与共同工作的署名。
作品与图像资料 ↗
从这种生产方式看，电影拍摄的并不只是一个被表演出来的故事。导演的位置、排练如何进行、人物之间怎样交谈，以及拍摄本身怎样改变现场，也进入了作品的问题范围。摄像机不是等到一切已经成立后才出现的中性见证者，它从一开始就是参与者必须面对的条件之一。
[2]
这使电影中至少存在两种不同的时间：现场中，人们尚不知道某次尝试将怎样结束；而在剪辑时，已经发生的结果成为可以被重新安排的材料。一个动作可以被剪成此前所有言语的终点，也可以与其他段落发生新的联系。一段等待可以被缩短，一次失败可以被保留，一句没有得到回答的话可以在很久以后才遇到回应。
57 / 《人类投降派》电影帧，01:02:32。叠化中的两个人；该图属于完成影片中的剪辑结果。
作品与图像资料 ↗
由此看，何发的剪辑工作与早期摄影拼贴之间存在可讨论的联系：材料都可以离开原来的位置，在新的邻接关系中形成意义。但两者又不能被等同。照片里的山与电影中的人，并不以同样的方式承担重新组织的后果。拍摄中的参与者仍然继续生活，作品则会以某个确定的版本反复播放。
58 / 《人类投降派》电影帧，02:05:00。白色围幕、灯光与身体共同构成的演出空间。
作品与图像资料 ↗
因此，集体创作不仅意味着“大家都贡献了素材”，还涉及谁能够决定材料如何被使用，谁能够对自己的形象提出异议，以及最后的电影如何容纳不同参与者对同一事件的理解。把导演的位置放进影像，并不自动解决这些问题，却可以使问题不再完全隐藏在作品之外。
59 / 《人类投降派》电影帧，02:26:59。《最后的排练》段落中的观众。
作品与图像资料 ↗
60 / 《人类投降派》电影帧，02:31:03。镜头朝向演出外侧的工作人员与记录设备。
作品与图像资料 ↗
《人类投降派》获得了2025年Esoteric Film Festival的最佳长片奖，官方获奖名单列出影片英文名及Fa He署名。这是一项可确认的影片获奖记录；而理解这部作品更重要的入口，仍是它如何把排练、相处、表演与剪辑组织成电影，而不是用奖项代替对其方法的说明。
[20]
10 /
档案与写作
重新阅读，也继续工作
何发的实践还有一个容易被放在作品之后、实际上却越来越重要的部分：记录与重新阅读。
P4留下的材料不只有演出照片与成片，还包括招募文本、创作宣言、排练记录、访谈、参与者回忆和项目反思。它们并不总是给出同一种解释。组织者可能记住一个项目如何成立，参与者可能记住某个难以接受的时刻，而后来完成的影片又会重新组织这些经验。何发的作品与文献网站，正在将这些不同类型的材料放入相互关联的阅读结构中。
[21]
61 / 何发作品与文献网站的写作目录，2026年10月8日页面截图。
作品与图像资料 ↗
这使档案具有一种超出宣传的用途。它可以让读者比较：最初的方案是什么，后来真正发生了什么，谁在当时作了怎样的表达，以及今天的解释与当年的记录是否一致。对于以现场和共同创作为重要部分的实践，这种比较尤其必要，因为作品并不能只由发起者事后的总结来代表。
《一个孔如何成为剧场》这样的回顾性写作，则尝试把摄影、语言和剧场之间的关系重新写出来。它的价值不在于证明所有早期作品都已经预告了后来，而在于让作者重新面对自己的选择：为什么希望别人进入作品，为什么不断要求“再来一次”，以及记录与剪辑究竟能够保留什么，又无法代替什么。
62 / 《人类投降派》影像与对白检索网站。2026年9月留存的界面。
作品与图像资料 ↗
正在形成的《关系生成影像论》进一步将这些问题转化为研究提纲。现有文本明确区分了镜头记录的事实、当事人的体验、关系的变化与电影形式带来的认识，并将相关命题保留为需要论证的问题，而非已经得到证明的统一理论。这样的区分有助于避免把“现场情绪很强烈”直接等同于“作品已经成立”，也避免把真实的经历当作艺术价值的自动保证。
[22]
近年的咔馆计划，则尝试把共同制作中的经验转向学习方法。其现有方法稿强调，从一个具体创作问题出发，经过尝试、拍摄、回看与修改，让参与者不只执行他人的决定，也能够作出选择，并看到选择带来的变化。它目前更适合被介绍为正在推进的工作方向，而不是已经获得验证的课程成效。
[23]
与此同时，新格物的研究使形态生成、材料与整体构造重新进入工作范围。这也再次说明，何发的实践并非不断抛弃旧媒介，而是在新的条件下回到尚未结束的问题。
[2]
63 / 《洞庭风细》表面细节，2012。摄影：何发；所摄灯具来自格物工作室共同实践。这是新格物研究回看的历史材料。
作品与图像资料 ↗
尾声 /
结语
做出作品，也面对作品不能替人完成的部分
何发的实践之所以不能只用“跨界”来概括，是因为跨越媒介本身并不构成其最有辨识度的工作。
真正具体的，是他反复采用又不断改变的那些做法：重新排列照片，让一座山在局部图像之间形成；把口音与误听留在转译过程里；让屏幕、座位和身体共同组织观看；把拍摄后的照片带到下一次见面；通过招募、排练、规则与记录，使尚未成形的工作获得发生的条件；再通过剪辑，把已经过去的现场变成能够被另一群人观看的电影。
这些做法并不相同，也不必被压缩成一个公式。但它们共同使创作从“作者表达自己”扩展到一个更复杂的范围：作品怎样形成，别人怎样进入，已经发生的东西又怎样被重新理解。
同时，何发并没有因为强调过程，就取消对作品形式的要求。一张照片仍然需要构图，一件灯仍然需要形体与材料，一场戏仍然需要时间和节奏，一部电影仍然需要选择、组织与结束。开放不能代替制作，共同创作也不能成为不作判断的理由。
也正因此，他的实践始终面对一项困难：既要把材料组织成一个有力量的整体，又要承认，进入这个整体的人并不能被作品完全解释。
从这一角度看，何发所持续工作的，不只是图像与现场之间的转换，也是作品的完成与关系的未完成之间的距离。
山可以重新拼合，影片可以再次播放；而人与人之间发生过的事情，不会因为一个版本被完成，就获得最后的解释。
64 / P4空间入口透出的光，2020。
本文依据截至2026年10月8日核对到的机构记录、同期项目文献、专业访谈、作品档案及现有研究文稿撰写。有关创作联系与方法意义的论述为本文分析；电影部分侧重生产方式与署名资料，不作为完整观片后的逐镜头评论。

HE FA / FA HE / 何发

何发，现用英文署名 He Fa；历史文献中的 Fa He 亦指同一位艺术家。何发在北京工作，创作摄影、影像装置、剧场与电影，并共同发起及长期主持 P4 剧场。
按作品在创作中的位置与代表性组织，并明确完成、研究进行中等状态。成形且有明确作者署名的早期作品、共同署名作品，以及有具体研究材料的当代项目，都可进入主要作品；早期探索、长期合作实践和提案文献分别阅读。

2013 / Archival inkjet print
Central
Placing the sun among the mountains rearranges a space that photography cannot ordinarily show.
Central, 2013. Image from the artist’s portfolio.
Artist
He Fa
Date
2013
Medium
Archival inkjet print
Dimensions
350cm × 200cm
The sun in a relief
Central began with an ancient relief encountered during a journey: the sun was carved into the middle of a range of mountains. He Fa brought that spatial relationship into photography, assembling fragments so that a sun ordinarily seen above the horizon could appear among the peaks.
A reorganized landscape
The work continues the photographic assembly of this period while organizing its composition around a specific formal problem. It offers a landscape constructed from multiple viewpoints rather than a single panoramic exposure. The portfolio records an inkjet print measuring 350 × 200 cm.
Looking closely at the sun’s position
The sun is small in the complete work; the portfolio preserves a separate view of that area. Orange discs sit among trees, mountain forms and overlapping photographs, making the artist’s idea of the center of the mountains visible as a compositional decision.
Where a centre is placed and where it is seen
The title Central specifies a place to look for, while dense photographic fragments repeatedly divert attention from it. A designated compositional centre need not coincide with what first catches the eye. Moving the sun into the mountain is the artist’s decision to rearrange pictorial relationships; the looking required to find it means that this decision is not immediately apparent.
Archive reading, 30 September 2026 · Site editorial interpretation, not an artist’s statement. Sources: He Fa Portfolio (PDF), p. 6. English is an editorial translation; document titles are translated where needed.
A high-resolution file linked to the work
The retained file center.tif measures 28,111 × 15,883 pixels. Its embedded preview and a sampled image correspond to the composition of Central on page 6 of He Fa Portfolio (PDF), connecting the portfolio image to a traceable high-resolution source. This correspondence is not a validation of the complete file and does not establish it as the sole or final exhibition output.
Archival file comparison · 30 September 2026. Based on the retained TIFF’s embedded preview, a sampled image and He Fa Portfolio (PDF), p. 6. English is an editorial translation.
ARTIST’S STATEMENT / PORTFOLIO
While travelling, I happened upon an interesting ancient relief in which the sun was carved into the centre of the mountains. For a photographer, the sun can only ever be above the horizon, so I placed it in the centre of the mountains too.
Translated from the artist’s Chinese portfolio statement.

If the sun moves, does photography’s promise change too?
Work date: 2013
Reading: 2026
Site editorial reading · AI-assisted · Version 2026-09-16
Begin with what happens in the work
The portfolio records a 2013 inkjet print, 350 × 200 cm.
The artist describes bringing the position of a sun seen in a relief into a photographic montage.
The sun is small, but the decision is large. Placed among the mountains, it becomes a new compositional centre. Photographs with separate origins serve a position that no single exposure witnessed. The work does more than manufacture a digital spectacle. It makes the differing spatial rules of photography and relief apparent: one luminous circle passes between media and changes how an image asks to be believed.
Central also challenges any simple story of relinquished control. It contains an unmistakable authorial decision: this element will go here. A landscape emerges not only from the contingent accumulation of fragments but from insistence on one placement. Pairing the work with Cocktail is more revealing than calling both photographic collage. One delegates position to a compositional idea, the other to file size. Different ways of exercising control coexist in the same year.
The limits of this reading
The artist’s account of the sun’s position is a creative proposition, not a law of astronomy or photographic optics.
Sources for this reading
Based on He Fa Portfolio 3, p. 6, and the published 2020 text What Is Shixiang?

sources.title: Cocktail
sources.text:
2013 / Archival inkjet print
Cocktail
Photographs taken while hiking are ordered by JPEG file size, allowing sky and ground to emerge from a digital sequence.
Cocktail, 2013. Image from the artist’s portfolio.
Artist
He Fa
Date
2013
Medium
Archival inkjet print
Dimensions
180 × 120 cm; 180 × 100 cm (two further works)
The “weight” of a photograph
Cocktail orders photographs according to the size of their compressed JPEG files. Images made in the mountains become files, then gather through sorting. The artist describes this as “settling or floating”: digital files appear to acquire material weight, and an arrangement of sky and ground emerges from their order.
Three images
The portfolio records three works titled Cocktail, all dated 2013. They share a procedure while forming different distributions of colour and image. They are presented here in portfolio order with their respective dimensions; no new numbers are added to the original titles.
Ordering files, reading a landscape
The three portfolio pages retain different degrees of separation between sky and ground: page 8 has a clearer blue-grey upper and green lower field; green and dark areas spread more widely on page 9; on page 10, a finer grid shifts from blue-black to brown-green. Small photographs remain legible as thumbnail views while forming bands of colour at a larger scale. Sorting supplies an arrangement; reading it as landscape also depends on habits of recognizing sky and land.
Archive reading, 30 September 2026 · Site editorial interpretation, not an artist’s statement. Sources: He Fa Portfolio (PDF), pp. 8–10. English is an editorial translation; document titles are translated where needed.
ARTIST’S STATEMENT / PORTFOLIO
Photographs taken while hiking are arranged according to their file sizes after JPEG compression. The photographs seem to acquire a virtual weight, like materials in the real world, and begin to settle or float. Sky and earth emerge naturally.
Translated from the artist’s Chinese portfolio statement.

Cocktail
What landscape appears when file size sets the order?
Work date: 2013
Reading: 2026
Site editorial reading · AI-assisted · Version 2026-09-16
Begin with what happens in the work
Photographs are arranged according to their file sizes after JPEG compression.
The portfolio records three works under the same title, with different dimensions.
Cocktail brings a usually hidden technical property forward. A photograph depicts something and occupies a number of bytes. That value depends on image information and compression conditions; it is not the actual weight of a natural scene. Once assigned an ordering task, however, it determines which photographs become neighbours. A machine-readable difference becomes a visual difference that viewers can read as sky, ground, settling or floating.
The procedure hands part of composition to a rule without removing the author. The selected photographs, compression settings and mapping from order to surface can all affect the outcome. The surviving statement does not specify those parameters, and a presentation should preserve that gap. The work opens a question about how judgment is delegated: instead of asking which photograph best resembles a landscape, one invents a condition and then looks at what it produces.
The limits of this reading
The original algorithm has not been established as reproducible. “Virtual weight” is the artist’s metaphor, not physical mass.

Based on He Fa Portfolio 3, pp. 8–10.

sources.text:
2017 / Language, video, printed text
Fafalish
A sentence passes through translation, accent and transcription, becoming a situation between languages.
Fafalish, CCA Simpson Library, San Francisco, 2017. Image: CCA/C Archives, CC BY-NC 4.0; compressed for the web.
HE FA’S ROLE
Artist and exhibition curator
LANGUAGE AS MATERIAL
Translation does not return meaning intact.
Fafalish was exhibited at CCA’s Simpson Library in San Francisco, October 2–December 15, 2017. It combined the video
Kunlun (Brother Order)
with printed text extending along walls and a column.
The process begins with Mao Zedong’s poem
Kunlun
: Chinese is translated word by word into English, spoken with a Chinese accent, heard as pinyin, transcribed into Chinese characters and translated into English by machine.
Reading the installation today, these shifts suggest that an utterance is shaped by every person and tool it passes through. The wall lets a visitor compare traces; the listening station asks for time. Accent and mishearing become material that can be examined, rather than simply errors to be removed.
SIX TRANSFORMATIONS / AFTER THE EXHIBITION ACCOUNT
01
Chinese poem
02
Word-by-word English
03
Accented speech
04
Heard as pinyin
05
Chinese characters
06
Machine English
Listening and reading meet at one station.
Successive transformations unfold on paper.
Exhibition photographs: CCA/C Archives,
CC BY-NC 4.0
. Resized and compressed for the web.
From language shifts to the space between screens.
Seen alongside YourTube (2018), Fafalish opens a question that later takes another material form: what has happened to the content before it reaches us? Fafalish exposes accent, transcription and translation. YourTube places images and comments within a space where people sit together. Both reward beginning with the installation and returning to the text.
Exhibition and original sources
CCA VAULT: exhibition record, photographs and curatorial statement ↗
The process account follows the exhibition record. The comparative reading on this page was written in 2026.
Between wall, column and listening station
The portfolio separately documents the listening station, long wall and column. Printed language takes on different spatial scales: visitors can pause at a tablet, follow sheets above the workstations or read at a column between bookshelves. A text frame from Kunlun on p. 33 places different languages and phonetic transcriptions alongside one another.
Translation takes place in front of the camera
Two vertical test recordings bring typography, images and a phone’s live translation interface into one chain of observation. “FUCK IS .mov” records separated English letters and changing translation results; “白眼1.mov” repeatedly frames a red image combining Chinese characters and a face. They show an ongoing adjustment among letterforms, image placement and recognition results.
The 27-minute, 16.8-second recording “MAH02831.MP4” moves from a group gathering and talking to operations among paper, phone and computer display. The original photograph “DSC02869.JPG” records this process at close range: handwritten and printed forms cover the table, the phone interface appears on a monitor, and participants converse in the same space as the screen.

Fafalish
If language cannot return intact, can communication still happen?
Work date: 2017
Reading: 2026
Site editorial reading · AI-assisted · Version 2026-09-16
Begin with what happens in the work
Exhibited at CCA’s Simpson Library from 2 October to 15 December 2017, including Kunlun (Brother Order) and installed paper texts.
The poem passes through literal English translation, accented reading, phonetic transcription, rewriting in Chinese characters and machine translation.
A deviation in one conversion becomes the material available to the next. Sound does not simply obey its source text, and written characters cannot guarantee a return to the original. Error is not a residue removed by final proofreading; it is an action that moves the work forward. Accent, guesswork, hearing and software rewrite meaning together. Looking only for what the final sentence means misses the way meaning acquires a body during its passage.
The library is not a neutral backdrop. Sheets along walls and a column turn a space associated with quiet, accurate reading into a site of successive transformations. The listening station moves visitors between written forms and sounds. The work does not prove that misunderstanding always liberates. More specifically, it disperses the authority to recognize, transcribe and correct a sentence beyond one standard language. Changing media becomes a way of changing the conditions of speech.
The limits of this reading
Machine mistranslation is not evidence of machine intention, and linguistic error does not establish a maker’s or viewer’s identity.

Co-initiators
Purples: Shen Bolun, He Fa and Shao Yifan
Development
Developed from Coliseum tests into a model within Purples
Documented practice
2021 calls for tests, assemblies and reflective writing
Giving the assembly the decision
Final Solution posits a fictional end-of-world assembly in which participants decide which roles may remain. The May test call allocated twelve deliberators and four candidates. Candidates made their case through non-violent means, and deliberators decided after questioning, discussion and voting. The theatrical “execution” meant elimination and departure. Rules for the June test, July questions and answers, and later discussions differ, documenting a model under revision.
In a signed article dated 14 July, He Fa recalls attending several assemblies and reflects on how the fictional situation prompted recurring questions about life and existence. He also describes a method of converting speech into text and preserving annotations and reflection. His 2022 retrospective identifies this work as a substantial event within Purples, co-initiated by Shen Bolun, He Fa and Shao Yifan.
The work as a collaborative practice
The work moves theatre from predetermined dialogue towards procedures collectively enacted and contested. Candidates’ accounts, deliberators’ reasons, the limits of rules and subsequent disagreements become material for later review. Participants retain their own experiences and words; He Fa enters through co-initiation, participation and reflective documentation.
Reading the versions
The project introduction and presentation proposal preserve different stages of the model. The fictional catastrophe’s deadline, roles and voting thresholds changed. Some documents specify a two-thirds majority among twelve seats; the presentation proposal specifies ten votes out of twelve. Each describes its own version of the game.
The Presentation Proposal places Coliseum alongside Duel Club and CCTV in a proposed continuous experience. The assemblies documented here and that later proposal retain their distinct status. The project trailer is a montage drawn from multiple scenes.
See the selected Project Introduction and source page 5 of the Presentation Proposal.

sources.text:
HE FA / 何发
LIN QINGXUAN RESIDENCY PROJECT · 2026 EDITION
Nobody's Return
森林记错了一个人
Does returning to a place
mean belonging to it again?
Moving-image installation / Spatial sound / Live performance
View an artwork still · window and forest
A white window frame and the forest beyond. A still from the work, not exhibition documentation.
01 / A WAY IN
Three minutes from the live performance.
Your browser does not support embedded video. Use the MP4 link below.
Three-minute edit · 03:00 · Chinese / English subtitles. He Fa reads the monologue and He Yu performs with a candle; at the end, they sit facing each other.
Compatible MP4 · 720p ↗
Watch on YouTube ↗
Explore the concept film · 2 min 48 sec
Watch on YouTube ↗
YouTube unavailable? Open the on-site player
2 minutes 48 seconds. Actual residency footage, two-channel excerpts and a sound schematic introduce the work, with Chinese and English text embedded in the picture. This is an entrance into the project, not documentation of an installed exhibition.
中文字幕 SRT ↓
English SRT ↓
中英双语 / Bilingual SRT ↓
02 / LIVE DOCUMENTATION
Candlelight, bodies and images on the walls.
He Fa reads into a microphone while He Yu raises a candle and turns among the viewers. At the end, He Fa and He Yu sit facing each other, with the candle between them. These six stills come from the live recording. Select an image to enlarge it.
He Fa reads from his phone into a microphone, with forest imagery projected behind him.
He Fa reads as He Yu raises her arms beside him, in front of a forest projection.
He Yu holds the candle in one hand and opens the other, with viewers behind her.
Seen from behind, He Yu extends her arm; candlelight remains between her and the viewers.
He Yu bends toward the candle on the floor, with viewers and projections behind her.
At the end, He Fa and He Yu sit facing each other, with the candle between them and viewers gathered around.
Open full-resolution image ↗
03 / IMAGE AND DURATION
The body leaves. Time remains.
Sizeng, Zengcheng and Yucen enter the same forest. Doors, paper, glass and water retain their passages without assembling them into one shared memory. After someone leaves, the space continues; a body in another image may still be waiting.
The work assigns no fixed past, present or future to its three figures, and day and night do not divide reality from dreaming. Long takes retain the duration of staying and leaving. Layers cross cuts: the next passage has begun before the previous one has left.
View two stills from the artwork
Body, paper and wall: contact leaves a trace, but the trace does not yield a complete story.
Two images occupy one plane: a layer continues across the cut.
Here, the Odyssey first means recognition after return, rather than a retold adventure. Does arrival let someone recognize home? If the place remains, does it recognize the returning person? The title keeps this unverifiable experience open, without making one ending answer for every body.
04 / A POSITION FOR THE VIEWER
Look toward one side and temporarily lose the other.
The following retains the two-screen and sound structure of the earlier Corridor V4 edition. It is presented separately from the live documentation above; the diagram does not reconstruct the recorded installation.
Each image plane loops for approximately one hour. The two sides form neither a panorama nor a complete answer. While the viewer faces one side, the other continues. Turning, approaching and missing become conditions of seeing.
Six spatial sound channels share a playhead and clock, looping independently over 37 minutes 17 seconds. Each wall also has its own sound. The unequal sound and image cycles change their encounters. A and B have equal image durations and do not drift once their start is fixed. These six custom sound positions are not cinema 5.1.
Schematic of facing image planes, viewer and six sound positions; not to scale

The single-screen web editions contain that wall’s picture and wall sound only, without the six-point spatial layer. Sound captions describe documented paper, cloth, water, rain and ambience. “Wall-sound pause” does not mean the whole installation is silent.
Wall A · excerpt from the one-hour loop
Continuous excerpt 02:00; source interval 04:20–06:20.
Sound captions for the full one-hour edition · VTT ↓
Wall B · excerpt from the one-hour loop
Continuous excerpt 02:00; source interval 03:20–05:20.
Sound captions for the full one-hour edition · VTT ↓
The excerpts come from different windows in the two walls and do not simulate synchronized A/B playback. The artist retains the full one-hour bilingual viewing copies and exhibition masters; contact for screenings and exhibitions.
05 / TEXT AND LIVE BODY
Can a memory leave the body it came from?
“One person’s leaving was recorded on another person’s waist. You only see it when they bend.”
Performance text, section 07
The thirteen-part monologue begins with coming back, yet cannot settle who has returned. Money, interest, calculation, consent, screens and bodies mingle; a pronoun changes position before its sentence ends. Chinese homophones and the changing meanings of 还 turn language itself into a site of recognition.
He Fa reads the thirteen-part text in the live performance. He Yu raises the candle, pauses and turns; her movement and He Fa’s voice keep their own rhythms. At the end, they sit facing each other. The relation between body and voice extends beyond a sentence-by-sentence correspondence.
Read all thirteen sections in Chinese and English ↗
中文原稿 TXT ↓
English translation TXT ↓
The Chinese preserves the original wording, line breaks and spacing. The English is an editorial translation for this edition; reading both keeps visible the sound relations that cannot fully translate.
06 / CONTINUITIES
Carry the question forward, not the forest.
Fafalish ↗
Translation, accent and transcription prevent language from returning unchanged. This monologue places that displacement inside a single speaker.
YourTube ↗
Connected seats and screens give viewing a bodily position. The two-screen corridor asks what one gives up seeing in order to see.
Human Surrender ↗
The person filming is also inside the relationship; the camera offers no final neutral position. Here, sound, image and body retain accounts that do not fully agree.
These are editorial connections proposed in this presentation, not claims that the works belong to one event.
07 / EDITION AND CREDITS
The work, its live realization and its editions.

Hamlet’s Mirror
Performers, projections and screens reflect one another as Hamlet is broken into shifting fragments.

HAMLET’S MIRROR · TIME AND RECORDS
Beyond the excerpt,
other durations remain.

He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang / FakingAosome, 2015.

An excerpt
03:48.08

Watch the 3:48 excerpt ↓

Recorded from one direction
34:54.509

Presented here as documentation.

Another record within the space
37:39.4

Presented here as documentation.
Co-creators
He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang / FakingAosome
Date
2015
Medium
Moving image, performance, projection
Duration in portfolio
Fragments of 15 seconds to 4 minutes; a 20-minute final version is also described
Taking the play apart
He Fa breaks Hamlet into short fragments. As he enters its roles, the image of a character is also separated from the body. Performance within a screen, images projected onto a person and the live performer’s movements form displaced relationships. The viewer encounters Hamlet in several times and positions.
Projection and performance
The original statement identifies the large screen, projection and performer as three interacting elements. Information originates in the performer’s own actions, then returns to the body through images. Occlusion, reflection and superimposition unsettle the division between a subject and its projected double. The work also carries questions of the whole and its parts from the earlier photographs into the time and space of performance.
Acts, sketches and moving images
The surviving sketches develop bodies, stairs, rooms and superimposed figures. English act sheets identify Walking, Father’s Ghost, Finding Mother, Asking, Mice Running, Manipulation, Ophelia Going Mad, and Hamlet and I. Sketches and act documentation are presented in portfolio order for comparison.
FakingAosome and the original version
The CAFAM proposal jointly signed by He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang on 5 September 2016 explicitly identifies Hamlet’s Mirror as the first project of FakingAosome, the group they founded in 2015. It records its development from June to December 2015 at P4 Theater in Beijing. This directly signed document supplies collaborative credits that were not detailed in the earlier individual portfolio.
From an excerpt to longer event recordings
Two “HAMLET’S MIRROR” exports in the working archive both run 3 minutes, 48.08 seconds, at 640 × 360 and 960 × 540 respectively. Four aligned visual samples correspond, and their complete decoded audio produces the same checksum. The records therefore connect them as different exports of the same excerpt.
Two longer files offer a different scale of viewing. “1-1-1我对面.mov” runs 34 minutes, 54.509 seconds and records figures and projections from one direction. “哈姆雷特的镜子1.mp4” runs 37 minutes, 39.4 seconds; sampled frames include a cubic space, projected text, images and bodies. These are the durations of the surviving files and do not establish that a performance was recorded in full.
Source documents: HAMLET'S MIRROR.mov; HAMLET'S MIRROR.mp4; 1-1-1我对面.mov; 哈姆雷特的镜子1.mp4.
The body as an interruption of the image
In Walking, body and shadow fall out of alignment; in Manipulation, clothing becomes a surface for coloured projection. Relations between roles are also formed through occlusion, projection and changes of scale. Earlier collages compressed different moments into one surface; here a body can interrupt an image and be covered by it again. The act-by-act documentation makes this distinction visible, though static documents cannot establish the rhythm of an entire performance or its audience’s response.
Archive reading, 30 September 2026 · Site editorial interpretation, not an artist’s statement. Sources: He Fa Portfolio (PDF), pp. 36–39; the “Theory Theatre” proposal, pp. 1 and 3. English is an editorial translation; document titles are translated where needed.
ARTIST’S STATEMENT / PORTFOLIO
In these short videos I reinterpret Shakespeare’s Hamlet. I dismembered the entire play into fragments that seem both familiar and unfamiliar. Of course you can say this has nothing to do with Hamlet; it is only my understanding of it. Hamlet, deferred into other people’s times and spaces, keeps changing roles. The characters cannot be defined precisely between the confused spaces inside and outside the screens. Through projection, reflection, concealment and occlusion, qualities that have blurred or disappeared seem to emerge again. I become the characters in these fragments, sharing their frenzy or sorrow. In an empty reality I look for the meaning of existence: “To be or not to be, this is a question.”
Translated from the artist’s Chinese portfolio statement.

When my image returns to my body, where is the character?
Work date: 2015
Reading: 2026
Site editorial reading · AI-assisted · Version 2026-09-16
Begin with what happens in the work
A jointly signed 2016 document describes the 2015 original as one screen, one performer, one projector and one video camera.
Hamlet is broken into short fragments; live body, screen and projection overlap and obstruct one another.
The figure on screen does not remain safely at a distance. When projection returns to the body, the performer carries an earlier self while present movement can block that image. Obstruction can therefore change where a scene takes place. The body is more than an instrument of emotional expression: it is a surface through which images appear, lose coherence and shift position. Viewers continually compare live action, recorded action and the location produced by projection.
The work shares the early montages’ problem of a whole made from several positions, but the medium changes its consequences. A photographic seam can be fixed; the intervening body renews the boundary from moment to moment. Shakespeare’s character becomes material for the two makers to divide, inhabit and address rather than an endpoint to reproduce faithfully. Presenting the original beside the four-screen proposal shows a spatial problem being rewritten, while keeping an unrealized plan distinct from exhibition history.
The limits of this reading
The duration of a surviving fragment is not the duration of a complete performance. Realization of the four-screen proposal is unverified.
Sources for this reading
Based on the 2015 portfolio and the CAFAM proposal jointly signed by He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang on 5 September 2016.

A FILM · 2023–2024

How the film took shape
The project moved through casting, rehearsal, filming and public performance in 2023; an approximately 156-minute film cut was completed in 2024.
Project statement
Human Surrender / Shoot Self with You took shape through casting, rehearsal and filming in 2023. Participants faced one another and the camera; initiating, performing, filming and directing intersected within a shared creation process.
At 19:30 on 26 August 2023, The Last Rehearsal took place at Ciyu Bookstore (Middle Theater branch). The final performance before filming wrapped combined theatre, performance art, live sound, installation, audience interaction and continuous photography; material from the event entered the film.
After completing the film, He Fa continued to work with its voices, dialogue, breath, images and excerpts through sound sessions, explanatory shorts and frame-by-frame notes.
A line through the work
When performers, director and camera all remain inside the relation, can looking stay neutral?
2023.06.03
June 2023: an initial three-part film proposal
He Fa’s recruitment text of June 3 proposed three parts: long-take rehearsals in a black stage space; a camera following performers into everyday life; and a public performance recording their interaction with an audience. Three people were sought to play a director and two leads, with work planned for June–August. This proposal documents an early method rather than the final film’s structure, cast size or duration.

2023.08.18
From a borrowed camera to shifting production roles
The production account of August 18 names Yun Jianhui as an early initiator and cinematographer. Zhou Jinsong and Liu Jinqi recorded the process while contributing ideas, scripts and production work. He Fa describes roles changing during the work: actors could direct, camera operators could perform, and recorders also acted within events. These contemporary credits preserve individual contributions alongside the shifting structure of the collaboration.

The pre-performance credits for The Last Rehearsal
The August 25 announcement scheduled the film’s concluding performance for 19:30 on August 26 at Ciyu Bookstore’s Inside-Out Theatre branch. It lists Huang Meng, Sun Jiarui and Xu Shuai as performers; Yun Jianhui as recorder; Zhao Xuan, Ru Meng and Zhao Ziyi as musicians; and He Fa as the behind-the-scenes producer. The plan combined theatre, performance art, live sound and installation, with camera documentation throughout. These are the roles stated in the pre-performance announcement.

CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
Human Surrender / Shoot Self with You
When shared experience becomes a film, who can still answer within it?
Work date: 2023–2024
Reading: 2026
Site editorial reading · AI-assisted · Version 2026-09-16
Begin with what happens in the work
The 2023 Last Rehearsal announcement links the public event to the film from the outset.
The end credits assign direction and writing to the team collectively; He Fa’s published 2024 account likewise describes performers working as directors, camera operators and writers.
The film overlays the reciprocal looking of rehearsal with the gaze of later viewers. Cameras are present from the outset, and people know their actions may become future images. The camera is therefore not a transparent witness outside the event. The collective direction and writing credits extend this relation into authorship; He Fa’s directing, initiating, producing and editing work forms a concrete part of that practice.
Editing still selects sequence, distance and duration; collective credit does not make those decisions vanish. The question is how the film lets voices continue to encounter one another and where it fixes a relation into one version. A published 2026 reading of eyes, sound, cameras entering the frame and questions offers entrances for close viewing. These remain versioned interpretations to be tested against passages in the film. It cannot simply become testimony that theatre has exposed real people, and a director character cannot automatically be equated with He Fa outside the frame.
The limits of this reading
The film, public performance, rehearsal records and 2026 research text remain distinct versions. Private experience is not inferred from characters or performances.

sources.title: I
sources.text:
2012 / Archival inkjet print
I
A macro lens travels across the body; individual photographs assemble into an enlarged self-portrait.
I, 2012. Image from the artist’s portfolio.
Artist
He Fa
Date
2012
Medium
Archival inkjet print
Dimensions
320cm × 320cm
Becoming a mountain
In I (2012), the photographer becomes the terrain being photographed. A macro lens attends to skin, facial features and hair, piece by piece; these close observations are assembled as a self-portrait measuring 320 × 320 cm. The grid divides a recognizable face and retains traces of its photographic construction.
Between near and far
From a distance, the image remains a face. At close range, it can be read as a surface composed of many details. A comparable shift occurs in the contemporaneous Shanshui works: both a landscape and a body invite repeated movement between the whole and its parts.
From skin detail back to human scale
After the full image, the portfolio places a macro photograph of skin beside an installation portrait. Pores, fine hair and skin become terrain; a person standing before the work restores its scale of 320 × 320 cm. The two distances correspond to the artist’s statement that “I became the mountain.”
Records from 2010 and 2012
The same portrait also appears in the 2010 Large Portraits portfolio as Portrait — He Fa: a vertical image without a grid, recorded at 2310 × 2430 mm. In the 2012 portfolio, I has a square, gridded composition and is listed at 320 × 320 cm. Dates and dimensions are retained from their respective documents.
My Face and the About Tangle process materials
Page 18 of the multi-artist Tangle document presents this self-portrait as “He Fa · My Face” with a bilingual statement. He Fa’s separate 23-page About Tangle presentation begins with photographs of Mount Siguniang and its rocks, moves into close observations of mouth, forehead, eyes, nose and ear, then returns to the complete face.
Page 17 gives the full portrait as 273 × 287 cm; pages 19 and 20 show details of skin and hair labelled at original size. Alongside the 231 × 243 cm record in the 2010 portfolio and the 320 × 320 cm gridded version of I from 2012, this preserves different documented dimensions and compositions for the portrait materials.
Source documents: 纠结（多艺术家文献）; 关于纠结——何发.
The grid and viewing distance
The heavy black grid becomes visible before the texture of the skin. It divides the face into stable regions and makes the person an object of inspection, cell by cell. At close range, pores, hair and reflected light can briefly displace recognition. Beside the ungridded portrait version, the change concerns more than scale: the frame makes the organization of looking part of the image.
Archive reading, 30 September 2026 · Site editorial interpretation, not an artist’s statement. Sources: Large Portraits — Works by He Fa, pp. 2–5; He Fa Portfolio (PDF), p. 2; the Struggle catalogue, p. 18. English is an editorial translation; document titles are translated where needed.

This is a huge photograph. I observed myself through a macro lens, from a mosquito’s point of view. The idea came to me while climbing a mountain: I became the mountain, and the camera became the me observing me.

I
When I become the terrain, who is looking at whom?
Work date: 2012
Reading: 2026
Site editorial reading · AI-assisted · Version 2026-09-16
Begin with what happens in the work
The 2012 portfolio lists a 320 × 320 cm inkjet print; other retained documents record different dimensions and compositions.
Macro photographs form a self-portrait; process material includes mouth, forehead, eye, ear and skin details.
ARTIST’S STATEMENT · PORTFOLIO EXCERPT
I became the mountain, and the camera became the me observing me.
Statement in the artist’s portfolio; distinct from this page’s interpretation
Prepared from page 2 of the artist’s retained portfolio, He Fa Portfolio 3. Chinese titles follow the source; English titles are translations for this site unless already given in English. Images retain their full composition. Dimensions refer to the version listed in that portfolio.
Editorial translation of the Chinese portfolio statement.
Check the work record and source documents ↗
This face has two competing scales. Recognizing He Fa from a distance means overlooking individual pores and hairs. Approaching a fragment makes the body’s material clear while personal identity temporarily recedes. The grid is more than a trace of montage technique: it prevents these two tasks from being completed at once. The viewer must choose a distance and acknowledge what remains invisible at another one.
The artist compares himself to a mountain and the camera to the self observing him. This division moves the self-portrait beyond the convention of expressing an interior life: one person can make the image and be the object it cannot encompass at once. The different recorded sizes and compositions should remain visible. They show that this “I” has more than one definitive-looking form: bodily material enters successive versions, placing stable identity beside the revisability of its image.
The limits of this reading
Different documented versions should not be collapsed into one dimension; the portrait does not establish a personality or psychological state.
Sources for this reading
Based on He Fa Portfolio 3, p. 2, and the Tangle / About Tangle documents identified on the public work page.

sources.text:
2014 / Any surface suitable for projection
Lose losing
An image experiment specified for projection on a surface at a variable scale.
Lose losing, 2014. Image from the artist’s portfolio.
Artist
He Fa
Date
2014
Medium
Any surface suitable for projection
Dimensions
Variable, determined by the exhibition space
From photographs to a projectable image
This 2014 work appears alongside the Wu images in the same portfolio, but its medium is specified as “any material suitable for projection,” with dimensions determined by the exhibition. That specification allows the image to leave a fixed print format and enter another surface and scale.
An even field of attention
Pale grey, orange and cyan particles lie densely together, with diffuse edges and no single centre. Looking can shift from finding an object to sensing density. Compared with the more distinct clusters in Touch touching on the following portfolio page, attention here moves more evenly across the surface. This page presents a portfolio still; the source page specifies neither a separate running time nor a particular installation.

Sangou GIF Theatre
A virtual character builds a theatre through repetition, transformation and brief pieces of language.

The still is the original first frame. Playing restores the original loop; it does not resume from the still’s position.
Public image accompanying I—a Sangou; original article byline: frankfaker.
Creative duo
FakingAosome: He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang
Early document
The team’s work list on page 1 of their jointly signed CAFAM proposal dated 5 September 2016
Later publication bylines
Five 2022 articles credited to frankfaker and aosome; original bylines retained
Building a theatre from a virtual character
A 2016 proposal jointly signed by He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang lists Sangou among FakingAosome’s works. It describes a “cyber-theatrical action”: using the internet to create a series of GIF images of a virtual character and collaging them into new theatrical and narrative spaces. The attribution comes from an explicit team work list, rather than assumptions about aliases or folder names.
In the public images, the simply drawn character repeats as a blue pattern, changes its posture in magenta lines and moves in loops against a green ground. A limited number of frames turns small gestures into fragments that can be watched again. Brief poems and wordplay add another voice to the figure. A body need not first stand on a physical stage: arrangement and timing themselves organise the encounter.
Connecting two sets of documents
Five public articles from August 2022 place Sangou alongside solo dance, Baudelaire, Hamlet and Guy Debord. Four are credited to frankfaker; A Sangou Dancing Alone is credited to aosome. The 2016 proposal establishes the work’s relationship to the duo, while each 2022 publication retains its byline. Aliases are not forced into one-to-one real-name matches, nor are all later images retrospectively dated to 2016.

sources.title: Shanshui
sources.text:
2012 / Photography, digital montage, light boxes
Shanshui
From a distance, a landscape. Up close, photographs made at different times and positions.
Viewing distance
Shanshui, 2012. Artwork image; open the project to explore it at high resolution.
HE FA’S ROLE
Artist
Year
2012
Medium
Photography, photomontage and large-scale image
Role
Artist
Tens of thousands of photographs are collaged and layered into a landscape. Move closer, then step back, to shift between fragments and the whole.
Enter the image
Explore Red, Green and White in full-resolution detail, with optional fullscreen roaming.
Explore / Auto roam ↗
07
Project statement
Completed in 2012, Mountain Beyond Mountains was He Fa’s graduation photography work. Photographing, dividing and recomposing organize many partial images into a landscape; it forms a whole at a distance and separates into time, viewpoint and fragment up close.
Mountain Beyond Mountains — Red and White entered the CAFA Art Museum collection. The work also established a line He Fa would return to: looking organizes space, bodies and relations.
A line through the work
If a landscape is made from countless incomplete views, do we see the mountain—or the way we look?
SCALE & COLLECTION
Navigate on screen; approach the physical work.
The museum record lists Red and White as C-print light-box transparencies and light boxes, each 110 × 190 cm, two works. At this scale, moving between individual photographs and the landscape becomes a bodily action. The online viewer offers another way to read closely.
Sources and version notes
中央美术学院美术馆 / CAFA Art Museum · 2012 ↗
ORIGINAL PROCESS ARCHIVE · AN INQUIRY INTO SHANSHUI
From photographs to brushstrokes: eight stages in the graduation defense
The original graduation defense, titled An Inquiry into Shanshui, records method studies, two approaches to arrangement and the final works. The eight illustrated stages below follow its order. Artist statements are translated from Chinese; the accompanying reading notes are editorial.
Since 2008, I have been trying to use photography to express the Chinese landscape in my mind. In the Shanshui series, I try to dissolve the photographs’ original content and information, turning them into “brushstrokes” in order to construct an ideal space.
He Fa, original graduation defense, p. 2. Translated from Chinese.
PROCESS 01 / 08
Movement through image shifts
Shifting the images brings changes in movement.
Artist statement · defense p. 4 · translated from Chinese
The initial experiment concerns the sense of movement in an image. The photograph ceases to act as a fixed window: shifts disturb its edges and details, changing the movement of the composition.
An Inquiry into Shanshui, graduation defense, p. 4. Full composition of the embedded image retained.
PROCESS 02 / 08
Scaling and displacement
Repeated scaling and displacement of the images produce an illusion between form and formlessness.
Artist statement · defense p. 5 · translated from Chinese
Scaling changes the relative size of the photographs; displacement lets a scene recur in different positions. The artist describes the resulting state as an illusion between form and formlessness: the landscape remains perceptible, but no single camera position accounts for it.
An Inquiry into Shanshui, graduation defense, p. 5. Full composition of the embedded image retained.
PROCESS 03 / 08
1,025 photographs and the trace of walking
I used 1,025 landscape photographs taken at Siguniang Mountain in Sichuan as material for experiments in forms of combination.
Because they were taken from different locations, each photograph has a different perspective. Combined, they move from the single-point perspective of conventional photography to a thoroughly dispersed perspective. This composition records the trace of my walking and my memory of the whole mountain.
Artist statement · defense p. 7 · translated from Chinese
The defense presentation specifies the number of source photographs and their location for this experiment. The figure 1,025 refers to this group from Siguniang Mountain; it does not establish the photograph count of every work in the series. The differences between camera positions matter: the route of looking becomes part of the composition.
An Inquiry into Shanshui, graduation defense, p. 7. Full composition of the embedded image retained.
PROCESS 04 / 08
First arrangement: a grid organized by color
The first method is an uncontrolled grid arrangement. I place the source photographs in the grid according to their color relationships, seeking only a faint distinction between ground, mountains and sky.
Artist statement · defense p. 8 · translated from Chinese
The grid first provides a framework for holding photographs. Color relationships then form broad spatial areas. A local image does not need to describe an identifiable place; the relation of ground, mountains and sky only needs to emerge faintly.
An Inquiry into Shanshui, graduation defense, p. 8. Full composition of the embedded image retained.
PROCESS 05 / 08
Working the grid: layers, shifts and opacity
I overlay and displace the photographs within each grid cell and change their opacity, allowing their content to recede. We seem to see ground, mountains and sky, yet also seem to see nothing.
Perhaps it is by dissolving representational forms in this way that the viewer’s inner feelings can be awakened.
Artist statement · defense p. 9 · translated from Chinese
At this stage, the recognizability of each photograph changes. Layering and opacity let specific scenes recede while the larger mountain form remains intermittent. The original statement tentatively links this dissolution to the viewer’s feelings.
An Inquiry into Shanshui, graduation defense, p. 9. Full composition of the embedded image retained.
PROCESS 06 / 08
Second arrangement: composing space subjectively
The second method is a freer arrangement under subjective control. It can better express my understanding of space.
Artist statement · defense p. 10 · translated from Chinese
A second route gives the artist more direct control over the positions and relationships of the photographs. The presentation places it alongside the grid method: one builds an overall field through cells; the other seeks space through subjective arrangement.
An Inquiry into Shanshui, graduation defense, p. 10. Full composition of the embedded image retained.
PROCESS 07 / 08
Reworking photographs into a shared atmosphere
I then rework each photograph again, seeking an atmosphere in which they permeate one another.
Artist statement · defense p. 11 · translated from Chinese
After arranging the images, the artist continues to work on them individually so that different views, scales and levels of transparency act together. Arrangement is an intermediate stage; the way images permeate one another is also part of the making.
An Inquiry into Shanshui, graduation defense, p. 11. Full composition of the embedded image retained.
PROCESS 08 / 08
Combining both arrangements
Finally, I tried overlaying the results of the two methods, creating a state of seeing mountains as mountains, then not as mountains, then as mountains again. Although the forms in each individual photograph are dissolved, the mountain’s form becomes more pronounced. This form is my experience in the mountains, my understanding and interpretation of them.
Artist statement · defense p. 12 · translated from Chinese
The final step overlays the results of both routes. Forms within individual photographs recede, while the mountain as a whole becomes more pronounced. The artist identifies this composite with experience, memory and interpretation in the mountains, rather than the reproduction of a fixed viewpoint.
An Inquiry into Shanshui, graduation defense, p. 12. Full composition of the embedded image retained.
VERSIONS AND COLLECTION RECORDS
Dimensions remain attached to their documented versions
The defense concludes with Shanshui—Red, Shanshui—White and Shanshui—Green (pp. 14–16). Its account of the making belongs alongside the later portfolio descriptions and institutional collection record.
On pp. 3–5, He Fa Portfolio 3 records Green, White and Red as works from 2012, each measuring 300 × 170 cm, made with backlit photographic film and a lightbox. These dimensions describe the versions listed in the artist’s portfolio.
The CAFA Art Museum’s
2012 graduate-work collection list
records Shanshui—Red and Shanshui—White as C-print backlit film and lightboxes. It gives the dimensions as “(110 × 190) × 2” and a quantity of two: Red and White together comprise two works, each 110 × 190 cm. This is the collection version.
Both sets of dimensions are preserved in their source contexts. The available documents do not explain the precise production, resizing or reprinting relationship between these versions.
Chapter sources
He Fa, original graduation defense, An Inquiry into Shanshui, pp. 2, 4–12 and 14–16; He Fa Portfolio 3, pp. 3–5; CAFA Art Museum, 2012 graduate-work collection list. Process images use the full embedded images from the presentation, without cropping. English statements were translated from Chinese for this archive.
Another early portfolio record
This early portfolio presents Shanshui through a horizontal landscape. Distant mountains, nearer trees and sky are joined from many photographs. Differences in brightness and scale are not completely smoothed away. The image retains both the broad shape of a landscape and traces of its construction; peaks, foliage and blocks of colour become visible at different distances.
In a preserved statement, the artist begins with the act of sorting photographs. He describes assembling more than a thousand photographs from a trip to Huangshan and relating this process to a moving viewpoint in landscape painting. The portfolios record different dimensions and media for Shanshui. Those differences are retained here as distinct records, rather than treated as a single exhibition specification.
Pages 14–15 of the 38-page portfolio record a 2400 × 1250 mm light box. Page 12 of the 13-page portfolio records 520 × 520 mm and mixed media. Both give January 2012. These are version records for Shanshui, not evidence of separate works.
Shanshui: Early Portfolio Record, 2012. Portfolio image 1 of 1.
The 2012 thesis: from modes of looking to photographic brushstrokes
Read alongside the graduation presentation’s process images, the 2012 thesis Exploring Shanshui Photography places the work between three modes of looking: shifting viewpoints in Chinese landscape painting, mobile viewpoints in David Hockney’s photocollages, and Cézanne’s late construction of a whole through patches of colour. He Fa translates these readings into his own method, treating photographs taken along a walk as elements of differing texture, light, darkness and colour.
Chapter Five again records an experiment using 1,025 photographs taken at Siguniang Mountain in Sichuan, superimposing gridded and subjective arrangements. The intended viewing moves between the whole and the detail: “The viewer experiences what I experienced, and feels what I felt.”
Beginning with photographs of Huangshan
In two early statements, He Fa recalls reassembling more than a thousand photographs taken during a visit to Huangshan while sorting his pictures. He noticed a resemblance between photographic assembly and a view that changes as one moves through a landscape. Finding that an imitation of this form was insufficient, he returned to nature and brought the experience of walking back into his work.
This recollection records an early experiment with Huangshan photographs. The graduation presentation separately documents an assembly experiment using 1,025 photographs of Mount Siguniang. The two sources retain the distinct locations and image counts associated with the initial attempt and the later methodological experiment.
Source documents: 作品自述（何发目录）; 作品阐释（照片目录）.
The graduation plan for three lightboxes
The undergraduate graduation guidance document names the project “An Exploration of Shanshui Photography,” records the proposal date as 26 December 2011 and lists Wang Chuan, Miao Xiaochun and Yao Lu as advisers. The plan specifies three photographs—Green, White and Red—presented as C-prints in lightboxes, each measuring 190 × 110 cm.
The guidance log records a discussion of the exhibition format on 1 March 2012 and of dimensions and proportions on 20 April. This plan for three works, the portfolio’s 300 × 170 cm version and the CAFA Art Museum’s collection of the red and white works belong to distinct records and stages.
Source documents: 本科生毕业设计指导书——何发.
From sketches to exhibition
The graduation plan divides the work into sorting existing landscape photographs, reading about painting, drawing and revising sketches, producing the green, white and red works, and then adjusting the images and making lightboxes. February through April are assigned to the three images, May to revisions and lightbox production, and June to exhibition. This planned rhythm shows image experiments, physical presentation and thesis discussion developing together.
Source documents: 本科生毕业设计指导书——何发.
Taking one photograph apart
The midterm presentation begins with a photograph of rocks and trees. It divides the image, shuffles the parts and turns recognizable scenery into elements of different light, colour and texture. A subjective, painterly arrangement reassembles them; layering and displacement then change their boundaries. Vertical and horizontal shaking and changes of scale follow, before the experiment expands to a mountain assembled from 1,025 photographs.
Source documents: 山水之求索——中期汇报, pp. 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.
Surviving files from the assembly process
Two TIFF working files in the Shanshui directory gather rocks, trees, sky, visitors and architecture at different densities. The horizontal image measures 2074 × 1179 pixels and the square image 5120 × 5120. Black gaps and repeated fragments remain in the source files. These studies show photographic fragments overlapping, leaving openings or interrupting continuous space before they form an overall landscape.
The group also includes Photoshop Large Document files. The headers of “huangshan3.psb” and “最终.psb” both record 30118 × 16942 pixels, while their byte sizes and sampled fingerprints differ. The archive retains them as separate working files. The two process images shown here are likewise kept distinct from formally exhibited versions.
Source documents: Screen Shot 2014-10-06 at 10.36.49 AM M01 Mosaic.tiff; 拼贴139 M01 Mosaic.tiff; huangshan3.psb; 最终.psb.
Three ways of organizing attention
Green organizes depth through flanking mountains and a pale valley. In White, tree trunks and a path into the snow establish direction. Red sets ochre peaks against a blue-grey sky. Rectangular fragments repeatedly cross these spatial boundaries: just as the eye reads an inhabitable landscape, blocks of colour and seams return it to the image surface. The three works offer different rhythms of looking, beyond variations in palette.
Archive reading, 30 September 2026 · Site editorial interpretation, not an artist’s statement. Sources: the artist’s retained He Fa Portfolio (PDF), pp. 3–5; An Exploration of Landscape Photography, pp. 11–14. English is an editorial translation; document titles are translated where needed.

Shanshui
Can a mountain hold many acts of looking at once?
Work date: 2012
Reading: 2026
Site editorial reading · AI-assisted · Version 2026-09-16
Begin with what happens in the work
The series uses photography, digital montage and light boxes; the records include red, green and white works.
The early thesis outline connects the experience of climbing, the limitations of a single viewpoint and the study of montage.
At a distance a mountain takes shape; nearby it breaks into separate acts of framing. The viewer’s movement is therefore more than an optional way to appreciate scale. It is a temporal mechanism: stepping back compresses differences into an image, while moving closer releases them again. Each photograph records something it once faced, but no individual photograph witnessed the final mountain. The whole is made and should not be mistaken for panoramic proof of a particular site.
The important issue is not an abundance of information but its redistribution through a medium. Climbing involves direction, resistance and duration; the image makes these available on one surface. Montage compensates for the single viewpoint while introducing a different loss. A presentation should therefore let viewers see the complete work, inspect details and return to the whole. An automatic tour can suggest one reading, but should not prescribe its only sequence.
The limits of this reading
Image counts and output versions need separate verification. Digital viewing does not reproduce the scale or transmitted light of the original light boxes.
Sources for this reading
Based on the public work page, portfolio and early landscape-photography thesis materials. Later theatre theories are not treated as the original motivation of the 2012 work.

Stage documentation published in the introduction to Shixiang, P4 Theater, 2020.
HE FA’S ROLE
Collaboration with Zhang Shaohua; theory, structure, framework and interpretation
PHOTOGRAPHY THEATRE / BEIJING
Make a portrait.
Then face it together.
Shixiang is a P4 Theater photography-theatre project concerned with one’s own image. Practice began in 2019; a public account of its format followed in 2020. Zhang Shaohua and He Fa developed it together. Zhang worked on recruitment and the practical encounters; He Fa’s 2020 account describes his contribution to theory, structure, framework and interpretation.
The published introduction traces a movement from conversation in a white room to photography on a dark stage. A large-format camera and lighting become objects within that stage. Participants subsequently return to view and discuss the photographs.
Read as a work today, the portrait extends across waiting, meeting again and speaking about an image. The relationship between photographer and subject continues beyond the shutter’s release.
PHOTOGRAPH / VIEW / RETURN
Eight and a half acts.
Odd acts: photographing
Acts one, three, five and seven centre on photography.
Even acts: viewing and expression
Acts two, four, six and eight return to the images through viewing and expression.
The 2020 account connects this sequence with the seasons. The final half-act remains open in the public description.
A room for conversation.
The stage where photography takes place.
Participants decide whether their photographs become public.
This choice is part of the original project account. It allows participation without requiring a person’s image to circulate before strangers. This page uses venue and working photographs already published by P4.
Set beside Shanshui, Shixiang shifts attention from the assembly within an image to encounters between people. Set beside Human Surrender, it offers a route into the relationships, waiting and expression that form during filming.

Shixiang
After the portrait is made, what position remains for its subject?
Work date: 2019–2020
Reading: 2026
Site editorial reading · AI-assisted · Version 2026-09-16
Begin with what happens in the work
Odd-numbered parts centred on photography, even-numbered parts on viewing and expression; this was the published structure.
The 2020 project description gives participants a decision about publication.
An ordinary portrait session often ends when the photograph is delivered. Shixiang instead makes the previous photograph the starting point for another meeting. A person faces a preserved self again, recognizing it or finding it strange. A fixed image and an ongoing life occupy the same structure. Meeting again neither updates the earlier photograph nor guarantees acceptance of its interpretation. Photography extends from taking an image into a relation that requires further response.
A crucial formal decision is that participation need not cost the immediate public disclosure of a portrait. Decisions about whether and when to publish enter the project’s agreement, preserving the possibility of remaining unseen by present viewers. A work may therefore have happened without proving itself through an accessible face. That matters for this portfolio: richness is not the same as opening everything. Presenting structure, space and the terms of visibility can be more faithful than filling a page with private portraits.
The limits of this reading
Eight-and-a-half parts, one thousand participants and a long-term museum were announced plans, not completed totals. This is not a current open call.

Touch touching
Coloured circles fill an image whose scale depends on the space of projection.

Artist

From photographs to a projectable image
This 2014 work appears alongside the Wu images in the same portfolio, but its medium is specified as “any material suitable for projection,” with dimensions determined by the exhibition. That specification allows the image to leave a fixed print format and enter another surface and scale.
Contact within the image
Green and blue-black gaps form channels between rounded orange-red clusters. The eye moves between coloured masses and their edges; contact can first be read as shapes approaching, crowding and separating. This tactile association arises from the visible image. The portfolio’s title and medium alone do not establish touch sensors or audience interaction. The source page also specifies neither a separate running time nor a particular installation.
Archive reading, 30 September 2026 · Site editorial interpretation, not an artist’s statement. Sources: He Fa Portfolio (PDF), p. 21. English is an editorial translation; document titles are translated where needed.
A corresponding Photoshop working file
The retained Photoshop file quan.psb contains a 23,622 × 23,622-pixel image. A sampled preview of its composite image corresponds to the arrangement of colour clusters and channels in Touch touching on page 21 of He Fa Portfolio (PDF). The file’s fixed pixel dimensions and the work’s stated variable projection dimensions are recorded separately. The sampled correspondence does not establish the complete layer contents or final-output status, nor does this file alone demonstrate animation or a realized exhibition.

EARLY CHAPTER / GEWU STUDIO / 2012–2013
Gewu Studio
Twelve Water Lamps. Water held in light.
Huanghe Niliu, from Twelve Water Lamps, 2012. Photograph by He Fa; lamp from the studio’s collaborative practice.
Archival photograph of the illuminated work.
Follow the water
↓
GEWU STUDIO
A passage from images to objects
First, the movement.
Then, a lamp.
Curves gather, separate and turn. Fine ripples follow larger folds. Light passes from within, revealing depth and shade across one continuous surface. A still object holds the gesture of moving water.
At Gewu Studio, photography, objects, space and communication shared the same room. For He Fa, this early chapter left a question that remains open: how can a way of seeing become something the body encounters?

↓

Step back, a whole movement.
Different scales of movement form a single body. Light reveals them while leaving darkness between the folds.
Photography by He Fa. The lamps belong to Gewu Studio’s collaborative practice.

Work and collaboration
Twelve Water Lamps took shape through Gewu Studio’s collaborative practice in 2012. Referring to Ma Yuan’s Twelve Views of Water, it used parametric modelling and 3D printing to turn water patterns into lighting forms. The work was exhibited at Beijing’s LiangDian Design Center from December 2012 to January 2013.
He Fa co-founded Gewu Studio in 2012 and served as its artistic director, contributing photography, conceptual development, form exploration and artistic direction. The photographs on this page are by He Fa and hold his inquiry into form, light and viewing distance.
